A system in which a model plans and takes actions, such as using tools, browsing or editing files, to complete a goal over several steps.
Research into making AI systems pursue the goals their designers and users intend, and behave safely when those goals are unclear.
The work of preventing AI systems from causing accidental or deliberate harm, from biased outputs to misuse and loss of control.
Association of Mutual Funds in India, the industry body that publishes monthly fund flows and SIP data.
Application supported by blocked amount: IPO money stays in the applicant's bank account, blocked, until shares are allotted.
Application-specific integrated circuit: a chip designed for one job, such as AI inference or bitcoin mining.
Additional Surveillance Measure: a list of stocks with unusual price or volume moves on which exchanges impose stricter margins and limits.
The instruction set licensed by Arm Holdings that powers almost all phones and a growing share of laptops and servers.
India's oldest stock exchange, in Mumbai, home of the Sensex.
The NSE index of the most liquid Indian bank stocks; heavily traded in derivatives.
The benchmark price for crude oil from the North Sea, used to price most of the world's oil.
Consumer price index: a measure of the prices households pay for a basket of goods and services, used to track inflation.
Central processing unit: the general-purpose processor that runs a computer's operating system and most software.
Cash reserve ratio: the share of deposits banks must keep with the RBI as cash, earning nothing.
Domestic institutional investor, such as Indian mutual funds, insurers and pension funds.
Dynamic random-access memory: the main working memory in computers and servers.
The Mumbai street where the BSE stands; shorthand for the Indian stock market.
Electronic design automation: the software, from firms such as Synopsys and Cadence, used to design chips.
Exchange-traded fund: a fund that trades on an exchange like a share, usually tracking an index or commodity.
Extreme ultraviolet lithography: the technique, using machines made only by ASML, that prints the finest features on leading-edge chips.
Futures and options: the derivatives segment of Indian exchanges, where most trading by value happens.
Foreign institutional investor; now officially foreign portfolio investor (FPI). Their daily buying or selling moves Indian markets.
Federal Open Market Committee: the Federal Reserve body that sets US interest rates, meeting eight times a year.
Field-programmable gate array: a chip whose logic can be reconfigured after manufacture.
Net selling of Indian shares or bonds by foreign portfolio investors; large outflows weigh on the rupee and indices.
Government security: a bond issued by the Indian central or state governments.
Gross domestic product: the total value of goods and services an economy produces in a period.
Nifty futures traded at GIFT City in Gujarat, an early signal of where Indian markets will open; formerly SGX Nifty.
Grey market premium: the unofficial premium at which IPO shares trade before listing. It is unregulated and often wrong.
Graphics processing unit: a chip with thousands of small cores, first built for graphics and now the workhorse of AI training and inference.
Graded Surveillance Measure: exchange curbs on stocks whose prices look out of line with their fundamentals.
Goods and services tax: India's nationwide indirect tax, with rates set by the GST Council.
High-bandwidth memory: stacked DRAM placed next to an AI accelerator to feed it data very quickly; a supply bottleneck for AI chips.
The newest generation of EUV machines, with a larger numerical aperture that prints even smaller features.
Initial public offering: when a private company first sells shares to the public and lists on a stock exchange.
How many times over an IPO's shares were applied for, reported separately for QIB, NII and retail portions.
The NSE's volatility index, derived from Nifty option prices.
Low-rank adaptation: a cheap fine-tuning method that trains small add-on matrices instead of all of a model's weights.
Multi Commodity Exchange of India, where gold, silver, crude oil and other commodity futures trade.
Massive Multitask Language Understanding: a multiple-choice test across 57 subjects, now close to saturated by top models.
The RBI's six-member Monetary Policy Committee, which votes on the repo rate.
An open standard, introduced by Anthropic, for connecting AI assistants to tools and data sources through MCP servers.
Gordon Moore's observation that the number of transistors on a chip doubles about every two years.
A short ceremonial trading session held on Diwali to mark the start of the Hindu new year.
The non-volatile memory used in SSDs, phones and memory cards.
Net asset value: the per-unit price of a mutual fund, calculated daily.
Non-banking financial company: a lender that is not a bank, such as Bajaj Finance.
Non-institutional investor, also called HNI: an individual applying for more than Rs 2 lakh of IPO shares.
Non-performing asset: a loan on which interest or principal has been overdue for 90 days or more.
Neural processing unit: a block of a chip specialised for AI calculations, common in phones and laptops.
National Stock Exchange of India, the country's largest exchange by trading volume and home of the Nifty indices.
Nvidia's high-speed link for connecting GPUs to each other inside a server or rack.
The NSE's benchmark index of 50 large Indian companies.
The NSE index of the 50 companies ranked just below the Nifty 50.
Offer for sale: existing shareholders, often promoters or the government, sell shares through the exchange or in an IPO.
The Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries plus allies such as Russia, which coordinate oil output.
Personal consumption expenditures price index: the US inflation measure the Federal Reserve targets.
Public sector undertaking: a company majority-owned by the Indian government, such as SBI, ONGC or Coal India.
Qualified institutional buyer, such as a mutual fund or bank; IPOs reserve a portion for them.
Qualified institutional placement: a listed company raises money by selling new shares to institutions.
Reserve Bank of India: India's central bank, which sets interest rates, manages the rupee and regulates banks.
An open, royalty-free instruction set architecture that anyone can use to design processors.
Reinforcement learning from human feedback: tuning a model towards answers that human raters prefer.
Securities and Exchange Board of India: the regulator of India's securities markets.
Systematic investment plan: investing a fixed amount in a mutual fund every month.
Statutory liquidity ratio: the share of deposits banks must hold in safe assets such as government bonds.
A listing on the small and medium enterprise platforms of the NSE (Emerge) or BSE, with lighter rules and higher risk.
Securities transaction tax: a small tax charged on every purchase or sale of shares and derivatives in India.
A benchmark that asks models to fix real bugs from open-source GitHub projects; widely cited for coding ability.
The BSE's benchmark index of 30 large Indian companies, India's oldest stock index.
Same-day settlement, offered as an optional cycle for a limited set of stocks.
Trades settle one working day after the trade date; India moved all stocks to T+1 in 2023.
Tensor processing unit: Google's custom AI accelerator, used in its data centres and rented through Google Cloud.
The yield on US government debt. The 10-year yield is a benchmark for mortgages and borrowing worldwide.
Unified Payments Interface: India's real-time payment system linking bank accounts through apps such as PhonePe, Google Pay and Paytm.
The Cboe Volatility Index, which uses S&P 500 option prices to measure expected volatility; nicknamed the fear gauge.
West Texas Intermediate: the US benchmark crude oil price.
Techniques such as TSMC's CoWoS that place chips and memory close together in one package; a key constraint on AI chip supply.
A large institution allotted IPO shares a day before the issue opens; their shares are locked in for a period.
A hypothetical AI able to match people across most intellectual tasks. There is no agreed test for it, so labs use the term loosely.
Software that performs tasks usually needing human judgement, such as recognising images, understanding language or making predictions.
The mechanism that lets a transformer weigh how relevant every other token is when processing each token.
The algorithm that computes how much each weight contributed to an error, so gradient descent knows how to adjust it.
One hundredth of a percentage point: 25 basis points is 0.25%.
A prolonged fall in prices; often defined as a 20% drop from a recent high.
A fixed test set used to compare models on a task. Scores can mislead when models have seen the test data during training.
The daily file an Indian exchange publishes with every security's open, high, low, close and volume.
A single large trade done in a special exchange window, often between institutions.
The return an investor earns on a bond at its current price. Yields rise when bond prices fall.
Free extra shares given to shareholders in proportion to their holdings.
A prolonged rise in prices; often defined as a 20% gain from a recent low.
Tax on profit from selling investments. India taxes short-term (STCG) and long-term (LTCG) gains at different rates.
Borrowing in a low-interest currency, such as the yen, to invest in higher-yielding assets elsewhere.
The intermediate reasoning steps a model writes out before its final answer.
The share of chips on a wafer that work. Low yields make new process nodes expensive.
A small die combined with others in one package to build a larger chip, instead of making one huge die.
The maximum a stock may rise or fall in a day, set by the exchange as a price band. A stock that hits it is said to be locked in the upper or lower circuit.
An AI agent that reads a codebase, edits files, runs commands and tests to complete programming tasks.
Shorthand for the processing power, usually GPUs or other accelerators, used to train and run AI models.
The field of AI that interprets images and video: recognising objects, faces, text and scenes.
The maximum amount of text, measured in tokens, that a model can consider at once, including the conversation so far.
Inflation excluding volatile food and energy prices, watched by central banks for the underlying trend.
A fall of 10% or more from a recent peak that is smaller than a bear market.
An agency's grade of how likely a borrower, such as a company or country, is to repay its debt.
A building full of servers, storage and networking. AI data centres need large amounts of power and cooling.
Machine learning with neural networks that have many layers; the basis of modern image, speech and language models.
Synthetic audio, image or video made with AI to show a real person saying or doing something they did not.
The electronic account in which Indian investors hold shares, kept with depositories NSDL or CDSL.
A generative model that learns to turn random noise into an image, video or audio clip by removing noise step by step.
Training a smaller student model to imitate a larger teacher model's outputs.
A cash payment a company makes to shareholders out of its profits.
A measure of the US dollar against a basket of six major currencies.
A company's profit divided by its number of shares.
A list of numbers that represents the meaning of a piece of text or an image, so similar items sit close together.
Tests that measure how well a model or AI product does on the tasks that matter to its users.
The day F&O contracts settle. Index expiries often bring sharp intraday swings.
Government rules that restrict selling certain technology, such as advanced chips or chipmaking tools, to some countries.
A semiconductor fabrication plant.
A chip company that designs chips but outsources manufacturing to a foundry, such as Nvidia, AMD or Qualcomm.
The overnight interest rate the US Federal Reserve targets; its main policy tool.
Further training a pretrained model on a smaller, specific dataset to adapt it to a task, style or domain.
Foreign currency, gold and other reserve assets held by the RBI, used to steady the rupee.
A large model trained on broad data that can be adapted to many tasks, rather than built for one.
A company that manufactures chips designed by others, such as TSMC.
One of the most capable models available at a given time, usually from a handful of well-funded labs.
Contracts to buy or sell an asset at a set price on a future date, used to hedge or speculate.
A transistor design in which the gate surrounds the channel on all sides, used at 2nm-class nodes.
AI that produces new text, images, audio, video or code from a prompt, rather than only classifying or predicting.
The optimisation method used to train neural networks: repeatedly nudging weights in the direction that reduces error.
A company's own forecast of future revenue or profit, which often moves its shares more than past results.
When a model states something false or invented with confidence, such as a fake citation.
A lightly regulated investment fund for wealthy and institutional investors that uses strategies such as short selling and leverage.
One of the largest cloud providers, such as Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud.
A basket of stocks tracked as one number, such as the S&P 500 or Nifty 50, used to measure the market.
Running a trained model to get an answer. Most of the cost of serving AI to users is inference, not training.
The rate at which prices rise across the economy, reducing what money can buy.
Fine-tuning on examples of instructions and good responses so a model follows requests.
Research into what happens inside a model, so its decisions can be understood and checked.
A prompt crafted to make a model bypass its safety rules.
Indian number units: one lakh is 100,000 and one crore is 10 million.
A neural network trained on vast amounts of text to predict the next token, which lets it answer questions, write and code.
How long a model takes to respond; often split into time to first token and tokens per second.
How easily an asset can be bought or sold without moving its price; also the amount of money available in the financial system.
A branch of AI in which systems learn patterns from data instead of following rules written by hand.
A company's share price multiplied by its number of shares: what the market values the whole company at.
A trading halt across the whole market when the Nifty or Sensex moves 10%, 15% or 20% in a day.
A model design in which only some sub-networks (experts) are used for each token, so a very large model costs less to run.
A model that handles more than one kind of input or output, such as text, images, audio and video.
The field of AI that deals with understanding and generating human language.
A model built from layers of simple connected units whose weights are adjusted during training to map inputs to outputs.
The monthly US count of jobs added outside farming, a closely watched sign of economic health.
A model whose trained parameters are published for anyone to download and run, even if its training data and code are not.
Contracts giving the right, but not the obligation, to buy (call) or sell (put) an asset at a set price.
When a model learns its training data too closely, including noise, and performs worse on new data.
The learned numbers (weights) inside a model. Model size is usually quoted in parameters, for example 70B for 70 billion.
A measure of how surprised a language model is by text; lower means it predicts the text better.
Shares a promoter has pledged as collateral for a loan; high pledging is a warning sign.
Training after pretraining, such as instruction tuning and RLHF, that turns a raw model into a helpful assistant.
The first, most expensive training stage, in which a model learns general patterns from a very large dataset such as web text.
Share price divided by earnings per share; a common gauge of how expensive a stock is.
Investment firms that buy companies, often with borrowed money, aiming to improve and sell them.
A label for a generation of chipmaking technology, such as 3nm or 2nm. Smaller numbers mean denser chips, though no longer a literal size.
The founder or controlling shareholder group of an Indian listed company.
The instructions and input given to a language model.
Writing and testing prompts to get more reliable results from a language model.
An attack in which text hidden in a document, web page or email tricks a model into ignoring its instructions.
A central bank buying bonds to push down long-term interest rates and add money to the financial system.
A central bank shrinking its bond holdings, the reverse of quantitative easing.
Storing a model's weights with fewer bits, such as 8 or 4 instead of 16, so it runs faster and in less memory at a small cost in quality.
A language model trained to work through a problem step by step before answering, trading time and tokens for accuracy.
A significant, broad decline in economic activity; often approximated as two quarters of falling GDP.
The date on which a shareholder must be on the company's books to receive a dividend, bonus or split.
Deliberately attacking a model or system to find harmful behaviour or security holes before release.
Training an agent by trial and error, rewarding actions that lead to good outcomes.
The rate at which the RBI lends to banks overnight; its main policy rate and a driver of loan rates.
Fetching relevant documents and adding them to the prompt so a model answers from that material instead of memory alone.
The rate at which the RBI borrows from banks, absorbing surplus money from the system.
An offer to existing shareholders to buy new shares, usually at a discount.
An asset investors buy in times of stress, such as gold, US Treasuries or the Swiss franc.
Observed regularities showing that model performance improves predictably as data, parameters and compute grow.
Training in which the data supplies its own labels, for example predicting the next word of a sentence. It is how language models are pretrained.
A material such as silicon whose conductivity can be controlled; also the industry's word for chips made from it.
When a company buys its own shares, reducing the number outstanding.
Borrowing shares and selling them in the hope of buying them back cheaper later.
A semiconductor material used for power chips in electric vehicles and chargers because it handles high voltages efficiently.
A compact language model designed to run cheaply or on a device such as a phone or laptop.
A cryptocurrency designed to hold a steady value, usually one US dollar, backed by reserves.
Slow growth combined with high inflation and often rising unemployment.
The RBI window where banks park surplus funds overnight; it sets the floor of the policy corridor.
Dividing each share into several, lowering the price per share without changing the company's value.
A hypothetical AI that far exceeds human ability in most fields. Some labs now name teams and goals after it.
Training on examples that come with the correct answer, such as images labelled with what they show.
Training data generated by models or simulations rather than collected from the real world.
A single chip that combines CPU, GPU, memory controllers and other parts, as in most phones.
Standing instructions set by the developer that shape how a model behaves for every message in a conversation.
The point at which a chip design is finished and sent for manufacturing.
A setting that controls randomness in a model's output: low values give predictable answers, high values give varied ones.
Spending more computation while answering, for example by reasoning longer, to get better results without retraining.
The unit of text a language model reads and writes, often a word or part of one. Prices and limits are counted in tokens.
The component that splits text into tokens and maps them to numbers before a model sees them.
A model's ability to call external functions or services, such as search, code execution or an API, and use the results.
The process of adjusting a model's parameters on data so that its outputs improve on an objective.
The neural network architecture, introduced in 2017, that uses attention to process whole sequences at once. Nearly all large language models are transformers.
The tiny electronic switch that chips are built from; modern chips hold billions.
A database that stores embeddings and finds the items most similar to a query; often used for retrieval-augmented generation.
Funding for young, high-risk companies in exchange for equity.
Building software by describing what you want to an AI coding tool and accepting its code with little manual review.
A thin disc of silicon on which many chips are made at once before being cut apart.
A model that learns how an environment behaves so it can predict what happens next; used in robotics, games and video generation.
The instruction set used by Intel and AMD processors in most PCs and servers.
A chart of bond yields across maturities. When short-term yields exceed long-term ones it is called inverted, often read as a recession warning.
